# UI elements

**Generated by `pnpm blocks` from `packages/shared/src/blocks.ts`. Do not edit.**

Everything the agent can put on screen is one of these. It never writes HTML, CSS,
colours or sizes: it picks what a thing IS, and the stylesheet decides how it looks.
That split is why a session of twelve sections reads as one website — and it is the
reliability engine, because a model that cannot emit a layout cannot emit a broken one.

Any block may also carry:

| field | what it does |
|---|---|
| `id` | a name, unique within its section. Named blocks are updated one at a time; the rule is all-or-nothing per section. |
| `supersedes` | `"002-margins/numbers"` — the block this one replaces. Published sections are sealed, so this is how a correction works. |

## Structure

What a page is made of at the top level.

### `heading`

The page's claim — the one sentence the rest of it has to earn.

```json
{"kind":"heading","text":"A wing flies by throwing air downwards"}
```

**Limits.** Exactly one per page, and it is the first block.

### `section`

A break inside a long explanation. A movement, not a second headline.

```json
{"kind":"section","text":"It is compression, not friction"}
```

## Words

Prose is the default, not the fallback.

### `prose`

A paragraph. The default, not the fallback — most answers are these.

```json
{"kind":"prose","text":"Lift is the reaction to a **mass of air** pushed down."}
```

**Limits.** Three inline marks and no others: **bold**, *italic*, `code`.

### `quote`

One sentence pulled out because it carries the point.

```json
{"kind":"quote","text":"Pilots call it the coffin corner."}
```

### `list`

Short items that belong together and have no second dimension.

```json
{"kind":"list","items":["Speed, which sets how much air arrives","Angle"]}
```

**Limits.** 2 or more items.

### `note`

The caveat or the gotcha, set aside from the argument.

```json
{"kind":"note","text":"Q2 is provisional.","tone":"warn"}
```

**Limits.** `tone` is `info` or `warn`.

### `code`

Literal text — a command, a file, an exact value. Nothing inside is interpreted.

```json
{"kind":"code","text":"npm run build","lang":"bash"}
```

## Numbers

Only when the content genuinely is that shape.

### `metrics`

Real numbers worth reading on their own, not a restatement of the prose.

```json
{"kind":"metrics","items":[{"value":"$4.2M","label":"ARR","emphasis":true},{"value":"18%","label":"Growth"}]}
```

**Limits.** 2 to 4 items; values are strings, so the agent controls the formatting.

### `chart`

A trend or comparison where the SHAPE of the numbers is the argument.

```json
{"kind":"chart","values":[3,7,12,9],"labels":["Q1","Q2","Q3","Q4"],"highlight":[2],"caption":"Margin by quarter"}
```

**Limits.** 3 or more values. Two numbers are a comparison, not a shape.

### `table`

Genuinely two-dimensional data. If one column would do, use a list.

```json
{"kind":"table","headers":["Altitude","Drag"],"rows":[["Low","High"]]}
```

**Limits.** Every cell a string.

## Shapes of an idea

For relationships prose has to work hard to describe.

### `split`

A real contrast: before and after, option A against option B.

```json
{"kind":"split","panels":[{"title":"Before","text":"…"},{"title":"After","text":"…"}]}
```

**Limits.** Exactly 2 panels. A third makes it a table.

### `flow`

An ordered sequence where the order carries the meaning.

```json
{"kind":"flow","steps":[{"label":"SYN"},{"label":"ACK","warn":true}]}
```

**Limits.** 2 to 6 steps.

### `figure`

A drawing, when a relationship is spatial and prose cannot say it.

```json
{"kind":"figure","src":"election.svg","caption":"Timeout promotes a follower"}
```

**Limits.** An SVG the agent writes beside the page. A viewBox is required, no width or height, and no colour may be named — only currentColor and the palette tokens.

## Interaction

The reader answers by touching, never by being asked to type.

### `choice`

A question the agent cannot proceed without an answer to.

```json
{"kind":"choice","id":"which-file","prompt":"Which one did you mean?","options":[{"id":"a","label":"report-2025.pdf","hint":"~/Documents · 2.1 MB"},{"id":"b","label":"report-final.pdf","hint":"~/Downloads · yesterday"}]}
```

**Limits.** 2 to 8 options, `id` required. The hint is what people decide by.

### `next`

The questions this page opened and did not answer. Clicking one asks it.

```json
{"kind":"next","items":["Why does gasoline stop at 9:1?"]}
```

**Limits.** 1 to 5, at most one per page, and it is the last block.

### `link`

A jump to another section. Rarely needed in one scroll.

```json
{"kind":"link","page":"002-costs","text":"Cost breakdown"}
```

## The app quartet

Workspaces only — a page is a record, and a record cannot act.

### `rows`  · workspace only

The list you scan and act on: an inbox, a file list, search results.

```json
{"kind":"rows","id":"inbox","items":[{"id":"m1","title":"Invoice #4821","meta":"Acme · yesterday","state":"unread","run":"mail show 4821","actions":[{"id":"arch","label":"Archive","run":"mail archive 4821"}]}]}
```

**Limits.** Up to 50 rows, `state` is unread/done/warn, at most 3 actions each.

### `fields`  · workspace only

The key/value header a detail view opens with.

```json
{"kind":"fields","items":[{"label":"From","value":"Acme"},{"label":"Received","value":"Tuesday 14:02"}]}
```

**Limits.** 1 to 12 pairs. More than a dozen facts is the detail itself.

### `form`  · workspace only

Inputs the reader fills and submits — the block that makes a workspace act.

```json
{"kind":"form","id":"reply","submit":"Send","run":"mail reply 4821","fields":[{"id":"to","label":"To","type":"text","value":"a@b.c"},{"id":"body","label":"Message","type":"textarea","rows":6}]}
```

**Limits.** 1 to 10 fields; types text, textarea, select, number, checkbox, date. Values reach the command as $FIELD_<ID> environment variables — never write them into it.

### `confirm`  · workspace only

The gate before anything irreversible or outward-facing.

```json
{"kind":"confirm","id":"send","prompt":"Send this reply?","detail":"84 words to billing@acme.com","confirm":"Send","run":"mail send draft"}
```

**Limits.** `detail` says exactly what is about to happen.

---

20 kinds. Inline, inside text, there are exactly three marks: `**bold**` names a term, `*italic*` stresses a word, `` `code` `` is an exact value. Nothing else renders.
